s: The Kalamalla inscription is associated with which ruler and date?
x: The Kalamalla inscription belongs to Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, also known as Dhanunjaya Varma, and is dated to 575 CE.
tq: Use the ruler–inscription–date association.
sec: Renati Chola inscriptions → ruler, language, date

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kalamalla inscription?
o: A fully available Telugu inscription written in geya style
A Telugu prose inscription that is not fully available today
A Sanskrit inscription in Dviradagati ragada style
A donation record issued by Satyaditya in poetic metre
x: The Kalamalla inscription of Dhanunjaya is in Telugu prose, but it is not fully available today.
tq: Distinguish the inscription by language, form and state of preservation.
sec: Renati Chola inscriptions → ruler, language, date

s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Erragudipadu — Punyakumara — geya style
2. Malepadu — Punyakumara — Dviradagati ragada style
3. Potladurthi — Dhanunjaya — first fully available Telugu inscription

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Erragudipadu is associated with Punyakumara and the geya style, while Malepadu is associated with Punyakumara and Dviradagati ragada. Potladurthi is also associated with Punyakumara, not Dhanunjaya, and the description of the first fully available inscription belongs to Erragudipadu.
tq: Start with the sure inscription–ruler pairs and eliminate the swapped pair.
sec: Renati Chola inscriptions → ruler, language, date

s: The Erragudipadu inscription of Punyakumara is described as being written in which style?
x: The Erragudipadu inscription is described as being in geya, or song, style.
tq: Identify the distinctive literary form associated with the inscription.
sec: Renati Chola inscriptions → ruler, language, date

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Renati Chola inscriptions is correct?
o: The inscriptions were written exclusively in Sanskrit until the eighth century.
Thirty-three Telugu inscriptions, mostly donation records, are listed in CDX.
All the inscriptions were royal genealogies and none recorded donations.
The inscriptions were found only in the coastal districts of Andhra.
x: CDX lists 33 Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions, most of which are donation records or dana sasanalu.
tq: Reject absolute wording and recall the number and character of the records.
sec: Renati Chola inscriptions → ruler, language, date

s: The 33 Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions listed in CDX were found mainly in which areas?
x: The records were found mainly in the Jammalamadugu and Proddatur taluks.
tq: Test the location rather than the inscription names.
sec: Renati Chola inscriptions → ruler, language, date

s:
Consider the following statements about the development of Telugu under the Renati Cholas:

1. They made Telugu a royal and legislative language.
2. Their records replaced the earlier use of Prakrit and Sanskrit.
3. From 575 to 848 CE, Telugu appeared in full prose sentences.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Renati Cholas gave Telugu official and legislative status, and the period from 575 to 848 CE saw Telugu used in complete prose sentences.
tq: Check whether all three statements describe the same linguistic transition.
sec: Renati Cholas - credited with establishing Telugu in Andhra's history

s: Before 575 CE, Telugu appeared in the available records mainly in the form of:
x: Before 575 CE, Telugu appeared mainly in names; complete prose sentences became characteristic from 575 to 848 CE.
tq: Use the chronological contrast between names and prose sentences.
sec: Renati Cholas - credited with establishing Telugu in Andhra's history

s: Who among the following was regarded as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line?
x: Nandivarma is identified as the progenitor of the Renati Chola line.
tq: Separate the progenitor from the founder and the last ruler.
sec: Ruler - period - contribution

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dhanunjaya Varma — founder and capital at Chimbapuram
Nandivarma — last ruler and capital at Peddachapalli
Punyakumara — progenitor and title Chola Maharaja
Elachola Maharaja — founder and Kalamalla inscription
x: Dhanunjaya Varma was the founder, son of Nandivarma, and ruled from Chimbapuram. The other pairs confuse different rulers and roles.
tq: Apply the founder–capital association and eliminate swapped roles.
sec: Ruler - period - contribution

s: Mahendra Vikramavarman, a Renati Chola ruler, was the:
o: Grandson of Nandivarma bearing the title Muditha Silakshara Navarama
Son of Punyakumara and author of the Kalamalla inscription
Last ruler of the dynasty bearing the title Chola Mahadhiraju
x: Mahendra Vikramavarman was the grandson of Nandivarma and bore the title Muditha Silakshara Navarama.
tq: Match the ruler with his genealogical position and title.
sec: Ruler - period - contribution

s: Punyakumara ruled approximately during which period?
x: Punyakumara's period of rule is given as 625–650 CE.
tq: Use the middle chronological option after identifying the ruler’s period.
sec: Ruler - period - contribution

s:
Which of the following inscriptions were associated with Punyakumara?

1. Potladurthi
2. Malepadu
3. Erragudipadu
4. Kalamalla

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Potladurthi, Malepadu and Erragudipadu are associated with Punyakumara. Kalamalla belongs to Dhanunjaya Varma.
tq: Find the ruler–inscription mismatch in the list.
sec: Ruler - period - contribution

s: The decline of the Renati Chola power began after the reign of:
x: Satyaditya bore the titles Chola Maharaja and Chola Mahadhiraju, and the decline began after his reign.
tq: Distinguish the ruler after whom decline began from the last ruler.
sec: Ruler - period - contribution

s: Which one of the following was NOT a title of Punyakumara?
x: Pormukharama, Purushashardula and Uttamottama were titles of Punyakumara. Chola Sthapanacharya was the title taken by Tikkana Choda.
tq: Find the title belonging to a different ruler.
sec: Claimed ancestry and titles of the Renati Cholas

s: The Renati Cholas claimed descent from:
x: The Renati Cholas claimed Suryavamsa Kshatriya descent from Karikala Chola, although their culture and administration were Telugu.
tq: Separate claimed ancestry from cultural and administrative identity.
sec: Claimed ancestry and titles of the Renati Cholas

s: Renadu Saptasahasra was so called because it consisted of approximately:
x: Renadu was also called Renadu Saptasahasra, referring to 7,000 villages.
tq: Recognise the numerical meaning embedded in the regional name.

s: Renadu lay principally in the area where which present districts meet?
x: Renadu lay where Kadapa, Kurnool and Chittoor meet, in the upper Pennar basin.
tq: Use the three-district location clue.
sec: Territory - Renadu → present districts, capital

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Renadu was situated in the upper Pennar basin and was also known as Renati Cholanadi.
tq: Distinguish the basin location from neighbouring regional areas.
sec: Territory - Renadu → present districts, capital

s: The capital of the Renati Cholas was:
o: Peddachapalli, in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa
x: The principal capital was Peddachapalli in Kamalapuram taluk of Kadapa. Chimbapuram was specifically Dhanunjaya's capital.
tq: Distinguish the dynasty’s capital from the founder’s capital.
sec: Territory - Renadu → present districts, capital

s: The Renati Cholas ruled approximately from the:
o: Third to the sixth centuries CE
Fourth to the seventh centuries CE
Fifth to the eighth centuries CE
Seventh to the tenth centuries CE
x: The Renati Cholas ruled from the fifth to the eighth centuries CE.
tq: Place the dynasty within the correct broad chronological range.

s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Pottapi Chodas — Pottapi, Kadapa
2. Konidena Chodas — Kammanadu
3. Nellore Chodas — Vikrama Simhapuri
4. Renati Chodas — Velanadu

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Pottapi Chodas were associated with Pottapi in Kadapa, Konidena Chodas with Kammanadu, and Nellore Chodas with Vikrama Simhapuri. Renati Chodas belonged to Renadu, not Velanadu.
tq: Identify the swapped regional association in the family list.
sec: Telugu Choda families → region

s: The Konidena Choda family was associated with which region and capital?
x: The Konidena Chodas ruled in Kammanadu, comprising parts of Guntur, Ongole and Bapatla, with Konidena near Narasaraopet as their capital.
tq: Combine the family, region and capital rather than recalling only one item.
sec: Telugu Choda families → region

s: Which of the following statements about the Konidena Chodas is correct?
o: They emerged only after the Kakatiya period and had no known ruler.
Their inscriptions belonged exclusively to the fifth century.
They were a branch of the Nellore Chodas founded by Tikkana Choda.
They began from the mid-tenth century and included Tribhuvana Mallachoda, also called Tenkanaditya.
x: The Konidena branch dates from the mid-tenth century and included King Tribhuvana Mallachoda, also known as Tenkanaditya.
tq: Use the period and ruler together to reject dynasty confusion.
sec: Telugu Choda families → region

s: Which Telugu Choda family was regarded as the foremost Telugu Choda clan?
x: The Nellore Chodas, associated with Vikrama Simhapuri, were regarded as the foremost Telugu Choda clan.
tq: Identify the superlative description in the family comparison.
sec: Telugu Choda families → region

s: The Velanati Chodas came to an end when:
o: Dhanunjaya Varma shifted the capital to Peddachapalli
Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola
x: The Velanati Choda line ended when Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola.
tq: Use the ruler–event trap to distinguish the end of a branch.
sec: Telugu Choda families → region

s: Who was the progenitor of the Nellore Chodas?
x: Bijjana was the progenitor of the Nellore Choda family, while Manumasiddhi I was its first king.
tq: Distinguish progenitor from first king and later famous members.

s: Which one of the following statements about Tikkana Choda is correct?
o: He was the court poet of Manumasiddhi II and wrote Purushartha Saramu.
He ended the Velanati Choda line by killing Mummadi Rajendra Chola.
He was the founder of the Renati Chola line and ruled from Chimbapuram.
He was the son of Manumasiddhi I, helped Rajendra Chola ascend the throne and assumed the title Chola Sthapanacharya.
x: Tikkana Choda, also called Tikkabhupati, was the son of Manumasiddhi I and took the title Chola Sthapanacharya after helping Rajendra Chola ascend the throne.
tq: Reject the swapped deed and title of a related historical figure.

s: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana served as minister and court poet to:
x: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana served as minister and court poet to Manumasiddhi II.

s: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana went to Kakatiya Ganapati seeking help against:
x: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana approached Kakatiya Ganapati for assistance against Vijayaganda Gopala.
tq: Match the petitioner, the ally and the opponent.

s:
Arrange the following stages in the political position of the Renati Cholas in chronological order:

A. Feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas
B. Emergence of Renati Choda, Bana and Vaidumba states in Rayalaseema
C. Feudatories of the Pallavas
D. Rule of the Banas and Vaidumbas after the Renati Cholas

Select the correct sequence.
x: The Renati Cholas were first feudatories of the Pallavas, later of the Badami Chalukyas; the Pallava–Chalukya conflict produced the three Rayalaseema states, after which the Banas and Vaidumbas ruled the area.
tq: Fix the first and last stages, then place the change of overlord in the middle.
sec: Relations with Pallavas, Badami Chalukyas and Eastern Chalukyas

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the relations of the Renati Cholas with other powers?
o: They were feudatories only of the Rashtrakutas.
They began as feudatories of the Eastern Chalukyas and later became Pallava feudatories.
They were first feudatories of the Pallavas and later of the Badami Chalukyas.
They were always independent and never served as feudatories.
x: The Renati Cholas first served as feudatories of the Pallavas and later became feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas.
tq: Test the sequence of political subordination and avoid the absolute distractor.
sec: Relations with Pallavas, Badami Chalukyas and Eastern Chalukyas

s: The Vaidumbas are particularly associated with the issue of:
o: Gold coins bearing only Sanskrit legends
Prakrit inscriptions from the Godavari delta
x: The Vaidumbas issued Telugu hero-stone inscriptions, also known as veerakal records.
tq: Identify the distinctive epigraphic practice of the Vaidumbas.

s: The Telugu epigraphic practice of the Renati Cholas was later taken up by the:
x: The Eastern Chalukyas later adopted the Telugu epigraphic practice associated with the Renati Cholas.
tq: Trace the transmission of an administrative and epigraphic practice.

x: Purushartha Saramu by Sivadevayya records the Kakatiya-period rule that a woman's property passed to her daughters and daughters' daughters.
tq: Use the author–work–legal rule association.

s:
The inscriptions copied during the June 2026 survey of the Nallamala Tiger Reserve included records of:

1. Pottapi Cholas
2. Eastern Chalukyas
3. Kakatiyas
4. Pallavas only

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The survey included records of the Pottapi Cholas, Eastern Chalukyas and Kakatiyas. Pallavas only were not identified as the relevant group in the survey description.

s: The historical significance of the Renati Cholas in relation to Telugu is best expressed by which statement?
o: They restored Sanskrit as the principal legislative language of Andhra.
They used Telugu exclusively for religious poetry and not administration.
They introduced Telugu into Andhra only after Nannaya's literary works.
They gave Telugu its first royal dignity several centuries before Nannaya.
x: The Renati Cholas gave Telugu its first royal dignity, approximately five centuries before Nannaya, by using it in royal and legislative records.
tq: Use the time comparison and the royal-administrative distinction.
